result:
There is a suspended, breathless quality to the hour just before the sun breaks the horizon. The world has finished dreaming, but it has not yet decided to wake. Down by the water's edge, the quiet ocean is the color of bruised slate, shifting lazily against the pilings of the old wooden pier. The air tastes of salt, wet cedar, and cold stone, a clean, sharp breath that feels untouched by human hands.

A solitary gull sits atop a rusted iron bollard, feathers tucked tight against the morning chill, entirely indifferent to the slow turning of the Earth. Out on the open water, the fog lingers in ragged ribbons, ghosting over the swells before dissolving into nothingness. There is no urgency here, only the steady, ancient rhythm of the tide pulling back pebbles with a hollow rattle.

Far off, the faint hum of a diesel engine begins as an early fishing boat navigates the harbor channel, its tiny red and bright green navigation lights blinking like drowned stars against the gray. A single thread of amber catches the edge of a cloud, subtle at first, then spreading slowly into pale peach and violet.

In this brief, sacred corridor of time, everything feels quietly forgiven. The mistakes of yesterday belong to a different lifetime, and the heavy demands of the approaching day have not yet found their voice. It is an open, empty canvas, stretching endlessly across the calm water, waiting for the golden light to finally declare the day begun.
